challenges.challenge: The finding 'no licence' may be an artefact of scanning only 35 files if the corpus is bigger.
challenges.resolution: CLOSED — the corpus_root was enumerated exhaustively (find -type f = 35) and the product tree separately; both were scanned.

challenges.challenge: CC BY 3.0 at skeleton:L6406 could grant rights over derived text.
challenges.resolution: CLOSED — the line attributes CC BY 3.0 to an upstream SPEC SITE being noted, not to the PIPD document; it is provenance metadata about an external spec.

challenges.challenge: Making the repo public already granted an implied licence.
challenges.resolution: CLOSED AS FALSE — no such doctrine is established; visibility is not a grant, and PIPD/LICENSE already states no licence is granted.

challenges.challenge: The proposal 'prepare an owner slot' is a non-action dressed as a deliverable.
challenges.resolution: PARTIALLY CONCEDED — the slot is only a deliverable BECAUSE the grant itself is owner-only; it is paired with two real agent-executable changes (explicit LICENSE refinement, machine-readable SPDX emission) so the round does produce a changed, checkable artefact.

challenges.challenge: Choosing SPDX LicenseRef-Proprietary is itself a licensing decision.
challenges.resolution: CLOSED — declaring 'no licence' explicitly is a documentation of the existing non-grant, not a grant; any actual licence NAME would be a grant and is left to the owner.

note: CH-04 partially conceded and answered by scoping the deliverable to the two real changes plus the slot.
